paper text.text: Choose one of these nonplanar completions. Its bridge has connected interior, since Lemma~\ref{r2:one-attachment}(ii) would otherwise give two single vertices whose triangle completion is planar. Retain a $K_{3,3}$ subdivision of the chosen completion. Since $B_b+cw$ and $B_d+aw$ are planar, the subdivision uses $bc$ or $ad$, respectively. Reduce the chosen bridge while retaining the subdivision, its connected interior and an interior neighbor at each attachment. In the other bridge, keep one interior component, delete the others and contract the retained component to one vertex. Its neighborhood is the full attachment triple by Lemma~\ref{r2:one-attachment}(ii). Both bridges keep their attachment sets, and their interiors remain connected through $w$, so this gives an allowed minor of $B$. The chosen completion stays nonplanar, and in the other three tests the bridge containing $D_b$ is still adjacent to all of $X$. Thus all four tests remain nonplanar, so minimality leaves $B$ unchanged. Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} lists every possible $B_b$ with attachments $b,c,w$, added edges $cw,bc$ and required edge $bc$, or every possible $B_d$ with attachments $d,a,w$, added edges $aw,ad$ and required edge $ad$. An original edge $bw$ or $dw$ may lie on the retained subdivision, so that segment is taken both as an edge and as a path with one interior vertex. The records in~\supp{E16} include both choices of the nonplanar completion. Each of the $156$ candidates has nonplanar $B$, a $K_5$ minor, a separating set of at most two vertices, or a proper nontoroidal minor, a contradiction.
